item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Oct 10, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Pilates in The HIVE Pollinator Garden — Sat Oct 10, 10:00 AM — The HIVE Tasting Room and Kitchen
item.description:
Build strength, improve flexibility, and reconnect with your body in this pilates mat class in the pollinator garden. This energizing, full-body workout combines mindful movement, core-focused exercises, and controlled breathing to leave you feeling stronger, balanced, and refreshed. All ages and abilities welcome! After class, each participant receives a refreshing glass of California Pomegranate Honey Hibiscus Cooler or a sparkling mead beverage. Bring your yoga mat, water and wear comfortable clothes. If the weather is too cool or too hot, we’ll practice indoors, among the honey drums. Hosted in collaboration with locally-owned Club Pilates Gibson Plaza!

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Oct 10, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sat Oct 10, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Jim Bruno's Songwriting Workshop — Sat Oct 10, 2:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description: Jim Bruno is a San Francisco Bay Area based published songwriter. He taught Songwriting at the Freight and Salvage in Berkeley and at Foothill College in Los Altos Hills both for 11 years. He’s also taught Songwriting Workshops at Chicago’s Old Town School of Folk Music, at Far-West Music Conference, at San Francisco State University’s High Sierra Campus and more. Songs he’s written have been recorded and released by Shawn Colvin, Chuck Prophet, Mary Lou Lord, Cliff Eberhardt, Thad Cockrell, Maurice Tani and Laurie MacAlister. As a performing songwriter he has performed with or opened shows for the following artists: Shawn Colvin, Timothy B Schmidt of the Eagles, Graham Parker, John Gorka, Charlie Musselwhite, Joe Ely, Greg Brown, Steve Forbert, Bill Morrissey, Big Twist, and Cliff Eberhardt. He’s performed at the Greenwich Village Folk Festival, the Udine Folk Festival in Udine, Italy and has toured five times in Europe. He also played bass, guitar and sang in the Shawn Colvin Band

item.description: It’s 1987 on Los Angeles’ legendary Sunset Strip, where the Bourbon Room is the heart of the rock-and-roll scene. item.title: Savor: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Robert Mondavi Institute - Sensory Building
item.description:
Join us for this quarter's Savor event: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat.
The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities.
The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including:
Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of DavisSam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development CorporationChutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in SacramentoModerator Ca

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Dec 17, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Dec 24, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Graduate Education Application Workspace — Mon Nov 16, 4:30 PM — South Hall
item.description:
Applying to Graduate or Professional School This Fall?
Don't feel like you have enough time to get your applications done? Come work on them with us.
We've reserved dedicated time and space for students who are applying to graduate and professional schools. You'll work alongside GSP, EOP, and USP students who are going through the same process—giving you time to focus, get questions answered, and make progress on your applications.
Each session gives you time to: Set a goal for what you want to accomplish that day Work on your applications with dedicated time and fewer distractions Ask questions and troubleshoot challenges as they come up Share ideas and problem-solve with other students going through the process Make progress on the application you've been putting off
On select days, we'll also have Pre-Grad/Law Advising, graduate and professional students, Graduate Studies representatives, and other campus resources available to provide guidance and answer questions.

item.title: Davis Farmers Market - Every Saturday from 8am - 1pm — Sat Dec 12, 12:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Experience the heart and soul of Davis every Saturday at the Davis Farmers Market in Central Park! 🗓 Every Saturday⏰ 8:00 AM – 1:00 PM📍 Central Park, Davis Shop fresh from the source with local farmers and vendors offering: 🥕 Fresh, seasonal produce🌻 Farm products🛍 Handmade crafts🥖 Fresh-baked goods☕ Coffee and hot food Whether you’re stocking up on locally grown ingredients, enjoying breakfast in the park, or simply soaking in the vibrant community atmosphere, the Davis Farmers Market is a beloved weekly tradition for all ages. Bring your family, support local growers and makers, and enjoy the bounty of our fertile region every Saturday!
Source: Davis Downtown

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Dec 16, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.description:

Oct 13 – Juan Tellez, Political ScienceOct 27 – Tina Law, SociologyNov 10 – Mike Oskin, Earth and Planetary Sciences

item.title: Día de los Muertos Doll Making Workshop (Davis) — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM — Blanchard Room
item.description:
We invite children ages 8 through 14 to join artist Ramona García for a Día de los Muertos doll-making workshop. Participants will be making and decorating traditional Mexican Lupita dolls. Ramona García will share the history of the Lupita doll as a beloved folk toy from Central Mexico and will guide the participants through the process of doll-making. Registration is required. The workshop is limited to 20 participants. Parents may accompany their children and help them during the workshop but materials will be provided for the children only.
You can register here or at the Children's Desk in person.
Source: Yolo Library
